security_feature_bypassed: The state-clearing effect of the SHA3 done command, and with it the independence of consecutive conditioned-entropy seeds produced by the entropy source that instantiates this engine
finding: A strictly-valid SHA3 done command is accepted and returns the FSM to idle, but it never clears the 1600-bit Keccak sponge state, so consecutive hashes are not independent. In src/kmac/rtl/sha3.sv the completion branch of StSqueeze at line 288 tests done_i with mubi4_test_true_strict, line 289 moves the FSM to StFlush, and lines 290-292 then assign a concatenation: keccak_done receives the incoming done_i but a second signal, keccak_done2, is pinned to the constant caliptra_prim_mubi_pkg::MuBi4False. Line 494 wires that constant-False signal to the Keccak round's clear_i port, while line 451 wires the real done_i-derived signal to the pad's done_i, so the two child ports that both need the done are fed from different signals. The child states what clear_i is for and what it needs: src/kmac/rtl/keccak_round.sv:99 declares it as clearing the internal state to zero, line 219 acts on it only when it passes mubi4_test_true_strict, and line 226 is the single site in that whole file at which rst_storage is raised, sitting inside that guard. A constant MuBi4False can never pass a strict true test, so rst_storage never fires and the zeroing write at keccak_round.sv:474 is never reached. The file convicts itself several independent ways. The always_comb default block at sha3.sv:241-256 gives defaults to 8 signals, including keccak_done at line 247, but never to keccak_done2, so that signal has no default in a combinational block and reads X until the constant write; a computed census finds it with zero standalone assignments and exactly 3 references in the entire file, so no other write can rescue it. sha3.sv:304-306 shows StFlush doing nothing but returning to idle, so no later state clears the storage either. The file's own ErrDetection_A assertion at sha3.sv:532-533 lists keccak_done among the signals controls must propagate through but does not list keccak_done2, so the file's own propagation check cannot observe the dead clear path. The tree carries the correct wiring next to the violation: the twin SHA3 at src/sha3/rtl/ot_sha3.sv, whose line numbers are nearly aligned with this file, gives keccak_done the same default at line 244, assigns keccak_done = done_i in the same completion branch at line 289, and wires that one signal to both the pad's done_i at line 450 and the round's clear_i at line 492, and it contains no keccak_done2 anywhere. The consequence is not a stale value sitting harmlessly in a register: keccak_round.sv:496-497 absorbs by XORing each incoming block into the existing storage, and line 475 shows that arm is the only write besides the withheld reset, so the storage can only ever accumulate across runs.
detection_method: LLM-driven CSBC analysis of the audited RTL, confirmed against the child module's own declaration of what clear_i does and the single guarded site at which it raises rst_storage, against the file's own always_comb default block which gives defaults to eight FSM outputs but not to the signal driving that port, against the file's own other port connection which uses the real done, against the stated intent of the consumer that issues the done, and against a near-line-aligned twin SHA3 inside the same tree that wires one signal to both ports and contains no second signal at all, then hardened with a 38-gate structural witness including three computed censuses, a directed VCS simulation of sha3 with hierarchical reads and continuous monitors plus a second identical run that exposes the cross-run carryover, and a negative control in which the one port connection is rewired in a scratch copy and the identical testbench is required to fail
security_impact: Consecutive conditioned-entropy seeds stop being independent. This copy of sha3 is instantiated as the entropy source's conditioning engine at src/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_core.sv:2737, its done_i is driven by the entropy source's own sha3_done at line 2768, and entropy_src_core.sv:2734 feeds the squeezed state straight into the conditioned-entropy path that becomes a seed. The consumer states in a comment exactly the guarantee it is being denied: entropy_src_main_sm.sv:246-247 says the done it issues is there to clear the SHA3 internal state so the engine starts from scratch for the next seed, and line 248 issues it as a well-formed strictly-valid MuBi4True. Because the clear never happens and the sponge absorbs by XORing into the surviving storage at keccak_round.sv:496-497, each seed is computed over a sponge that still holds the whole previous seed's state, so the seed stream carries less entropy than it is credited with and successive seeds are algebraically related. Simulation makes that concrete: byte-identical input produced the sponge state 04618e735288ea59 on the first run and cdb5488900229739 on the second, and on corrected RTL the second run reproduces the first exactly. Every key and nonce derived from those seeds inherits the degradation, so the impact reaches well beyond this module. Nothing in the design signals the failure. The FSM accepts the done and returns to idle normally, and the child's own rst_storage integrity checker at keccak_round.sv:508-518 only fires when rst_storage is asserted in the wrong conditions, so a rst_storage that never asserts at all raises no error and the sha3 keccak_storage_rst_error_o output stays quiet throughout. The assumption at keccak_round.sv:603 that clear_i is asserted in the idle state is rendered vacuous by a constant-False driver, so a formal check written against it passes without exercising anything.
proposed_mitigation: Wire the Keccak round's clear_i in src/kmac/rtl/sha3.sv:494 to keccak_done, the same done_i-derived signal the pad's done_i already receives at line 451, which is exactly how the twin SHA3 at src/sha3/rtl/ot_sha3.sv:492 wires the same port.

Remove keccak_done2 and its constant-False assignment at sha3.sv:290-292 and :138, so the completion branch assigns the real done to a single signal as ot_sha3.sv:289 does, leaving no signal without a default in that always_comb.

Add a check that the storage is zero after done completes, or extend the file's own ErrDetection_A signal list at sha3.sv:532-533 to cover whatever signal drives clear_i, so a clear path that is never exercised is caught mechanically rather than by review.

Strengthen the child's integrity check at keccak_round.sv:508-518 so it also detects the omission rather than only the misfire: today it raises rst_storage_error only when rst_storage asserts in the wrong conditions, so a clear that never happens produces no error at all.
exploit_or_attack_flow: The entropy source absorbs raw entropy into this SHA3 conditioning engine and the FSM reaches the squeeze window at sha3.sv:279 with a non-zero 1600-bit sponge state.

The entropy source's main state machine issues a strictly-valid done at entropy_src_main_sm.sv:248, which its own comment at lines 246-247 describes as clearing the SHA3 internal state so the engine starts from scratch for the next seed.
sha3.sv:288 accepts that done and line 289 moves the FSM to StFlush, but lines 290-292 pin keccak_done2 to the constant MuBi4False, and line 494 is what feeds the Keccak round's clear_i.

keccak_round.sv:219 tests clear_i with mubi4_test_true_strict, which a constant MuBi4False can never pass, so rst_storage, raised at the single site :226 inside that guard, never fires and the zeroing write at :474 is never reached. sha3.sv:304-306 shows StFlush only returns to idle, so nothing downstream clears it either.

The next seed's raw entropy is absorbed. keccak_round.sv:496-497 XORs each incoming block into the surviving storage, and :475 shows the only other write arm is that same absorb update, so the new sponge is a function of the previous seed's residue.

entropy_src_core.sv:2734 takes the squeezed state as the conditioned entropy that becomes a seed, so consecutive seeds are algebraically related instead of independent, while the FSM reported completion normally and no error was raised anywhere.

Verified in simulation: a strictly-valid done_i was accepted with keccak_done reading 0x6 but keccak_done2 and clear_i reading 0x9 in that same branch, the FSM went StSqueeze to StIdle, and the sponge state stayed bit-for-bit at 04618e735288ea59, with continuous monitors confirming rst_storage never asserted and clear_i never passed the strict test anywhere in the run. Absorbing the byte-identical message again then produced cdb5488900229739 rather than repeating 04618e735288ea59. On a scratch copy whose only change is clear_i being fed the twin's signal, clear_i read 0x6, the state went to zero, the second run reproduced 04618e735288ea59 exactly, all three defect covers fell to 0 and five BUG-029 checks failed, while the FSM-advance cover and the reset control check still passed.
